source.author: verg
source.text: Linquimus Ortygiae portus, pelagoque volamus, bacchatamque iugis Naxon viridemque Donysam, Olearon, niveamque Paron, sparsasque per aequor Cycladas, et crebris legimus freta consita terris.
source.text_original: Linquimus Ortygiae portus, pelagoque volamus, / bacchatamque iugis Naxon viridemque Donysam, / Olearon, niveamque Paron, sparsasque per aequor / Cycladas, et crebris legimus freta consita terris.
source.text_english: We leave the harbor of Ortygia and fly over the sea, over Naxos, wild with bacchic revels on its heights, and green Donysa, Olearon, and snowy Paros, and the Cyclades scattered through the sea, and we skim the straits planted thick with islands.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: freta concita terris post Rhodum et Lyciam tandem uidit Cyprum, ubi sancti et uenerabilis Epiphanii genibus prouoluta decem ab eo diebus retenta est non in refectionem, ut ille arbitrabatur, sed in opus dei, ut rebus probatum est.
reuse.text_original: freta concita terris post Rhodum et Lyciam tandem uidit Cyprum, ubi sancti et uenerabilis Epiphanii genibus prouoluta decem ab eo diebus retenta est non in refectionem, ut ille arbitrabatur, sed in opus dei, ut rebus probatum est.
reuse.text_english: Stirred up by the seas after Rhodes and Lycia, she finally saw Cyprus, where, having thrown herself at the feet of the holy and venerable Epiphanius, she was kept by him for ten days, not for refreshment, as he supposed, but for the work of God, as the event proved.
